description: SuperAwesome AwesomeAds publisher SDK (tv.superawesome.sdk.publisher:superawesome, real code in the superawesome-base AAR). A kids-focused, COPPA/kidSAFE-certified ad SDK found in Outfit7's Talking Tom/Angela titles and Subway Surfers. The public API is a set of static-method facades — AwesomeAds.init(...) for setup, and SAInterstitialAd / SAVideoAd (static load/hasAdAvailable/play, keyed by integer placement id), the SABannerAd FrameLayout view, and the managed.SAManagedAdView (MRAID/HTML) view for ad operations. All results are delivered through the SAInterface.onEvent(int, SAEvent) callback. API is readable (Kotlin, unobfuscated) and stable across the 8.x-10.x range.

methods.name: init
methods.note: Main SDK init. 4 static synchronized void overloads: init(Application|Context, boolean[, Map<String,Object>]) -> void. Stubbing this disables SDK bootstrap; there is no init-completion listener, so no callback hang here

methods.name: load
methods.note: 7 static void overloads load(int placementId, ..., Context[, String][, Map]) -> void. Prefer stubbing load so no ad is ever fetched or cached. Results normally arrive via SAInterface.onEvent; once load is a no-op, neither adLoaded nor adEmpty/adFailedToLoad fires (see callback-hang note in protected_patterns)

methods.name: hasAdAvailable
methods.note: static hasAdAvailable(int) -> boolean; false is the natural 'no ad' state once load is stubbed, so callers gating play() on it take the no-ad path

methods.name: play
methods.note: static play(int, Context) -> void; launches the SAInterstitialAd display activity. Belt-and-suspenders with the manifest disable of that activity

methods.name: load
methods.note: 7 static void overloads load(int placementId, ..., Context[, String][, Map]) -> void. Stubbing prevents any video ad fetch/cache. Same callback consideration as SAInterstitialAd.load

methods.name: play
methods.note: static play(int, Context) -> void; launches SAVideoActivity

manifest_components.note: Fullscreen video ad activity (label SAFullscreenVideoAd); present in the superawesome-base 8.x and 10.x manifests

Interstitial display activity. NB this class name is dual-role: it is both the static load/play API facade AND the fullscreen Activity component. Disabling the manifest component only affects the Activity; the static methods are neutralized separately in ad_operations

protected_patterns.reason: onEvent(int, SAEvent) is the single callback bridge through which the SDK delivers every ad event (adLoaded, adEmpty, adFailedToLoad, adShown, adEnded, adClosed, ...) to the app's listener. It must never be stubbed. Callback-hang risk: because load is stubbed to return-void, the SDK never fetches an ad and therefore never fires ANY onEvent result — neither adLoaded nor adEmpty/adFailedToLoad. Apps that gate flow on hasAdAvailable() (returns false) or simply skip when no adLoaded arrives are unaffected; an app that shows a blocking 'loading ad' UI and waits for a load result event before continuing could hang. If that is observed, revert SAInterstitialAd/SAVideoAd/SAManagedAdView load stubs and instead disable only the display activities + play(). Not auto-targeted (no deep_patterns), listed as a guard for package-wide sweeps
SAInterstitialAd.getAd(int)/SAVideoAd.getAd(int)/SABannerAd.getAd() return the SAAd model object; returning null could NPE if a caller dereferences it. Not an ad-fetch trigger, so leave working
getListener()/getListener(int) return the SAInterface the app registered; returning null would break the app's own event handling. Object-returning getter, not an ad operation
Static getFeatureFlags() returns a FeatureFlags object the app may query; returning null could NPE. Object-returning getter, harmless once init is stubbed
